players.product: Cloud services for AI-related demand, Hy family foundation models (Hy3) and in-house AI compute infrastructure (IT equipment and data-centre capex)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 segments (Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell / CFO John Lo): total revenue RMB 204.8 billion, up 11%, 'with social networks contributing 16%, domestic games 23%, international games 9%, marketing services 21%, and fintech and businesses services 30%'. Value-added services revenue RMB 98 billion, up 8%: social networks up 1% to RMB 32 billion (long-form video subscriptions down 6%, audio subscriptions up 8% with Ximalaya, whose acquisition was completed in May); domestic games up 17% (Delta Force, Valorant PC, Valorant Mobile, Roco Kingdom: World); international games down 1%, up 4% in constant currency. Marketing services up 22% to RMB 44 billion on higher eCPM and impressions; FinTech and Business Services RMB 60 billion, up 9%. Gross profit RMB 118.4 billion, up 13% (VAS gross margin 64%, up 4 points; marketing services 57%; FinTech and Business Services 52%); R&D up 35% to RMB 27.2 billion; non-IFRS operating margin 36.9%, and 42% excluding new AI products; about 116,000 employees.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue RMB 204.8 billion (+11%); VAS RMB 98 billion (+8%); marketing services RMB 44 billion (+22%); FinTech and Business Services RMB 60 billion (+9%)

quarterly_data.signal: Tencent Cloud (Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell): 'while we're still working through capacity constraints, our cloud revenue growth rate accelerated from high teens percentage year-on-year in the first quarter to low 20s percentage in the second quarter', helped by AI-related demand (GPU rental, Model-as-a-Service, WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy token usage), international expansion and higher usage and pricing for general cloud services. Toward the end of the year and into next year Tencent will have 'sufficient GPU ASIC capacity' to step up renting out bare-metal GPUs and Model-as-a-Service. With input costs, particularly memory, rising, Tencent increased prices across the board for Tencent Cloud in May and has been reducing discounts more substantially; the China cloud pricing environment 'is not as difficult as it has been in the past.'
quarterly_data.figure: cloud revenue growth from high teens % (Q1) to low 20s % (Q2) year-on-year; Tencent Cloud prices raised across the board in May

quarterly_data.signal: AI compute capex (CFO John Lo / President Martin Lau / CSO James Mitchell): operating capex RMB 51.8 billion, up 190% year-on-year and 66% quarter-on-quarter, to support Hunyuan model enhancements, inference needs, AI capabilities across products and growing external cloud demand; non-operating capex RMB 1 billion. President Martin Lau: the AI-native capex is 'a lump sum that we are going to be investing this year and next year' and should not be assumed every year; further inference compute investment depends on returns; the lump sum is measured against cash, the investment portfolio, operating cash flow and prudent debt capacity. Compute from prepayments and orders made a couple of months earlier could now be sold 'at more than 30% profit compared to the price that we paid', and the infrastructure could be rented out at cost recovery or better via Tencent Cloud as a fallback. CSO: the primary use of the capex is training bigger Hunyuan models, the secondary is inference for Hunyuan, DeepSeek and other models behind WorkBuddy; capital allocation is dynamic, potentially steering more cash to capex and less to buybacks.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 operating capex RMB 51.8 billion (+190% YoY, +66% QoQ); non-operating capex RMB 1 billion

capex.display: AI-native capex a lump sum over this year and next

quarterly_data.signal: Hunyuan models (President Martin Lau): average daily token usage of Hunyuan 3's production version is about 6x that of the preview version across all channels; Hunyuan 3 is 'a very small model, even in today's terms' that matches or beats much larger models. Tencent is training a larger-parameter model, Hunyuan 4, 'which we expect to release later this year', then Hunyuan 5, and is scaling reinforcement learning and upgrading multimodal capabilities; management is confident Hunyuan will reach state-of-the-art level. Owning the model gives better unit economics through co-design of applications, model and compute.
quarterly_data.figure: Hunyuan 3 daily token usage about 6x the preview; Hunyuan 4 expected later this year

quarterly_data.signal: AI products (President Martin Lau / CSO James Mitchell): WorkBuddy orchestrates multiple agents and gives access to over 70,000 skills from Tencent Cloud SkillHub, with high retention and willingness to pay; gross margins for paying WorkBuddy users and for Model-as-a-Service are already comparable to Tencent Cloud overall, while free users are subsidized. Spending on new AI products went from RMB 8 billion in Q1 to RMB 10.5 billion in Q2, reprioritized toward WorkBuddy as it broke out. WorkBuddy is a multi-model platform: Hunyuan is one of its models, and its inference also serves DeepSeek and other models. Most WorkBuddy user spending is subscriptions, so the substantial ramp in cash receipts will reach Tencent Cloud's reported revenue through the year. Xiaowei, the agent inside Weixin powered by the WeLM model, will roll out in phases; its cost envelope will be less than the ongoing Yuanbao investment of the past year.
quarterly_data.figure: new AI product spending RMB 8 billion (Q1) to RMB 10.5 billion (Q2); over 70,000 SkillHub skills

quarterly_data.signal: Advertising outlook (CSO James Mitchell): in-app advertising games such as Arrows contributed about 2 percentage points to marketing-services revenue growth in Q2 (and would have added 4 percentage points to international games growth); growth 'will continue to tick up and tick down' and should not be straight-lined, as the China consumer and advertising market 'remains choppy', but Tencent expects to keep outperforming the market by a substantial margin with AI ad targeting, rising Weixin Video Accounts engagement (total time spent up over 20% in Q2) and a move toward closed-loop advertising.
quarterly_data.figure: in-app advertising games about 2 percentage points of Q2 marketing-services growth; Video Accounts time spent up over 20%
